Quick triage update:
- What I see so far: simultaneous increase in short-lived spikes of concurrent requests from Acme's webhook IP range beginning 15:03 PDT. Many of those requests include rapid retry patterns (client SDK configured with low backoff + 3 retries).
- Symptoms: routing layer queueing saturated a small subset of pods, causing timeouts upstream. As the routing layer timed out, some requests were retried by the SDK, creating a feedback loop (retry storm).
- Notable gap: our combined 5xx+429 rate alert is currently set at 25% over 10m; we should have a multi-signal alert that triggers earlier for correlated latency + quota exhaustion.

Immediate mitigation steps executed (15:40–16:00):
1) Scaled the downstream replica set by +30% for the impacted model variant (temporary emergency scale).
2) Applied a conservative circuit-breaker on requests from Acme's IP range (120s cooldown).
3) Enabled request sampling and added extra logging for 429->5xx transitions.

Next steps (owner assignments below):
- Short-term: confirm end-to-end recovery for Acme (Sean)
- Mid-term: patch routing rate-limiter config so throttles return 429 instead of causing backend overload (Marissa + Rishi)
- Long-term: runbook updates and SDK guidance for partner backoff defaults (Jonas + DevX)

I'll keep this thread updated.

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acme-payments.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: triage notes + immediate mitigations (ACME)

Post-triage technical notes: deeper findings and temporary mitigations we applied at 17:58 PDT.
Root cause (contributing factors):
- Customer traffic pattern: A large webhook batch from Acme caused a burst ~15:03. Their SDK retried aggressively on transient failures (0.5s backoff * 3 retries) which amplified load.
- Routing config regression: a recent routing change (rolled last week) reduced the token-bucket limit heuristics for short-lived bursts; under load we observed queue overflow and sudden connection resets which surfaced as 5xx from downstream services.
- KV cache pressure: the payload patterns caused frequent attention/KV cache eviction patterns on hot shards which increased p99 latency when cache misses fired.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back the routing token-bucket tweak to prior stable config (17:40) — dropped 5xx by ~65% in the next 8 minutes.
- Emergency scale: +50% capacity in the affected AZ for the next 90 minutes.
- Temporary IP-based ingress throttling for Acme to a safe-per-second rate to allow graceful backoff.

Metrics snapshot (15:00–17:00 PDT):
- Peak ingress for Acme: +420% relative to baseline
- System-wide 5xx spike: peak 20% (15:06), down to 3% after rollback and scale (17:48)
- Observed p95 tail: 420ms -> 980ms at peak; returned to ~420ms after mitigations

Follow-up recommendations (owner: Rishi & Marissa):
1) Routing layer: add a dedicated throttle path that returns 429 fast (and logs the throttle reason) to avoid backpressure into downstream pods.
2) Alerting: introduce a correlated alarm that looks at: ingress spike (>3x baseline), 5xx rate >8% AND p95 latency >2x baseline, with a 2-minute window.
3) Runbooks: add a checklist for partner-driven retry storms including steps to apply IP-based throttles, rollback routing changes, and emergency scale commands.
4) SDK guidance: work with DevX to publish recommended backoff defaults and to instrument SDKs for backoff jitter.

I will follow up with a short postmortem draft by tomorrow morning outlining timeline and code/config patches.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Capacity & Performance

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident debrief and action tracker (ACME)

Summary:
Thanks for the quick responses over the weekend. Root cause was a combination of a customer-induced traffic burst with aggressive client retries + a routing token-bucket regression that allowed queueing to overload downstream pods and surface as 5xx. The immediate mitigations (rollback + emergency scale + IP throttle) restored service within ~2.5 hours.

Key follow-up action items (owner — ETA):
1) Routing fix: ensure throttles return 429 and do not cause queue-overflow; add unit/integration tests for token-bucket heuristics (owner: Rishi; ETA: 3 business days).
2) Alerting: implement correlated multi-signal alert (owner: Marissa; ETA: 2 business days).
3) Runbook: add a partner-retry-storm runbook with exact shell commands, dashboard links, and escalation steps (owner: Jonas + DevX; ETA: 5 business days).
4) SDK guidance: publish partner-backoff best practices and recommended SDK defaults (owner: DevX; ETA: 7 business days).
5) Capacity planning: evaluate reserve capacity and automated burst policies for top 10 partners; present proposal to Ops leadership (owner: Sean; ETA: next Wed).

Rachel: I'm sorry for the disruption. We'll share the postmortem draft and a remediation timeline by EOD tomorrow and coordinate any SLA/credit conversations directly. Please let me know if you'd like a follow-up sync with our SRE/Platform leads this week.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (link above), acme_error_snippets.log

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
